title: CausalDub
subtitle: Replacement-Aware Video Dubbing for Diverse Sources
summary: CausalDub separates visual evidence that should be preserved from articulation that must follow replacement speech, then transfers that response to a two-evaluation causal editor.

domains.name: HDTF
domains.description: Studio and interview footage with replacement speech.

domains.name: TalkVid
domains.description: Web-video appearance, motion, and recording conditions.

domains.name: CausalDub-Bench
domains.description: Source-disjoint generated speakers from the frozen benchmark.

ablations.title: Reconstruction alone is not replacement control
ablations.description: A matched teacher intervention compares the same-audio-only control with replacement-aware refinement. Aggregate cross-audio Sync-C improves by 0.954–1.653 across the four frozen benchmarks; fidelity changes are reported separately.

ablations.title: DMD recovers compression-induced quality loss
ablations.description: Matched two-step trajectory regression raises FVD from 8.91 to 10.84; distribution matching lowers it to 7.76. DMD is used for quality recovery, not claimed as the source of replacement control.

long_form.title: Long execution exposes what short clips hide
long_form.description: The source-reanchored system bounds generated-state propagation at window boundaries. The continuous-cache control is shown as a limitation: it develops late visual degradation and is not used to claim persistent causal stability.

limitations: SyncNet confidence is not treated as proof of phoneme correctness; independent recognition is reported separately.
Source-reanchored 60-second execution does not establish drift-free persistent generation.
The benchmark does not cover arbitrary generator out-of-distribution behavior or universal fidelity superiority.
